A1.justification: Both complete, readable 36-page PDFs describe the same WIND watermarking work. Sections 1–7, Appendices A–J, equations, tables and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark-detection, attack-robustness, image-quality and runtime experiments, including Table 1 and Appendices D, G and H.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results, including watermark-detection comparisons, robustness analyses and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, secret-salt noise generation, Fourier group identifiers, WINDfast/WINDfull detection and the inpainting extension are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same prompt collection and MS-COCO-2017 data, synthetic and non-synthetic watermarking tasks, and transformation, reconstruction, steganalysis and regeneration attack scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including Tree-Ring/RingID in Table 1, the additional methods in Table 16, and SSL/StegaStamp in Table 15. The newly cited Gunn et al. work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The Stable Diffusion settings, 50 generation/inversion steps in Section 5.1, attack parameters, key/group configurations, metrics and appendix evaluation protocols remain identical.

E4.justification: The inference-step and group-count analyses, iterative regeneration tests, group-identifier distortion analysis and additional attack evaluations were already present in v1 and are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Mean and standard-deviation reporting in Tables 2 and 4 and the statistical discussion in Section 3 are unchanged. No repeated-run, uncertainty or statistical-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative images are unchanged throughout both papers. For example, Table 1 retains WINDfull2048 average accuracy of 0.969, Table 3 retains WIND FID of 24.33, and Table 14 retains 100% detection after 50 regeneration iterations.

T1.justification: The diffusion-inversion mathematics, Theorem 4.1, its cryptographic assumptions and the proof in Appendix E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: distortion-free initial-noise watermarking, efficient two-stage detection, robustness against removal and forgery, and extension to non-synthetic images.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations in Section 6 and Appendices C and F remain unchanged, including reliance on private model weights, editing-versus-forgery concerns, computational costs and distortion tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Implementation details in Appendix I and hardware/runtime information in Appendix H are unchanged. Section 5.1 repairs the pointer to already-present Appendix I without adding technical disclosures or changing resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gunn, Zhao and Song's An undetectable watermark for generative image models (2024) to the bibliography and an existing citation group in Appendix B. This is a limited citation addition without substantive rewriting of research positioning.

P1.justification: The running header changes from Preprint to Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025. v3 also replaces the unresolved Section 5.1 reference with Appendix I and corrects Table 11 caption punctuation; the narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 11's stray period beside the table is moved into its caption, slightly adjusting table alignment. The added reference causes limited bibliography reflow, and headers are updated. Figures and table structures are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: Repairing the Section 5.1 pointer to Appendix I improves navigation to implementation details, while the Table 11 correction and additional related-work citation modestly improve presentation and citation coverage. The scientific methods, evidence, theoretical support and limitations remain unchanged, so the gain is limited.
